title: Article page
brief: This is the page where Simon's published writing is read, at /blog/<slug> on the public website, and its one job is comfortable long-form reading on a 375 pixel phone and on a 1440 pixel desktop. Readers arrive from a shared link, the blog index or the homepage, mostly on a phone, and read one essay of about eight minutes from top to bottom. The page opens with the category, the publication date, the title, a one-line standfirst and the reading time, then an optional cover image, then the body: a lede, then sections that each start with an h2, with paragraphs, links, an ordered list, a blockquote and images. Body paragraphs are body copy and carry the primary text colour; only the kicker, dates and captions use supporting greys, all through Alfons typography tokens. Images arrive as sanitised HTML with natural sizes from 192 by 256 to 2160 square; each one is sized to its content, never upscaled past its natural width, never taller than the viewport, and a caption that follows an image as an emphasised paragraph is shown as that image's caption. The page has two floating companions that must never cover a word of text at either width: the section contents, which today is a fixed left rail of dots with labels, and the site-wide 'ask scheherazade' agent pill, fixed bottom left at roughly 190 by 40 pixels, which this page cannot change and must leave room for. The 'Back to Blog' link is also fixed today and likewise must not cover text. After the body come related articles and comments, which keep their content but may change their layout. The fixture is the real article 'I'm building a personal agent' (fixture.json beside round.json), which on the live site renders its 192 by 256 logo as an 883 pixel red block and lets the rail and pill overlap the opening text on a phone. Dark is the only colour mode, and the page takes its whole look from Alfons tokens and components, with LongreadHero, LongreadProse, LongreadProseSection, LongreadArticle and LongreadFigure as the existing parts to reuse before inventing any.

approaches.title: Quiet column
approaches.direction: Reduces the page to one centred reading column with no raised sheet and no fixed elements at all: the contents become an inline list under the standfirst, and the back link sits in the flow, pushing restraint and typography as the whole design.

deviations.what: Overrides LongreadProse's image rule from the page (:global .longread-prose img: width auto, max-width 100%, max-height 80dvh) and centres figures with their captions.
deviations.why: LongreadProse sets every img to width 100%, which upscales the 192 by 256 logo into a column-wide red block; the library has no natural-size, viewport-capped figure rule for sanitised HTML. Production fix belongs in LongreadProse, not in the page.

deviations.what: Steps LongreadProse body paragraphs and list items up from --text-body to --text-lead, and zeroes LongreadHero's own top and bottom padding, both through :global from the page.
deviations.why: The direction makes typography the whole design: lead size gives about 45 characters a line on a phone and near 65 at the 36rem desktop measure, and the in-flow back link already opens the column, so the hero's 48px top band would double the space. Neither component exposes a size or spacing prop.

deviations.what: At 375 wide the site's agent pill still sits over a body paragraph mid-scroll (shoot.mjs reports DIV.agent-pill-stand-in at the logo position).
deviations.why: With no fixed or sticky element of its own, a full-width scrolling column cannot keep text from passing beneath a pill fixed bottom left at roughly 187 pixels wide on a 375 pixel screen. The page clears it at the opening screen and at the end of the page (a 96px floor under the end matter); keeping it clear while scrolling needs a page-owned floor or dock (approach a5) or a change to the pill, both outside this direction.

approaches.title: Sheet with an outside rail
approaches.direction: Keeps the raised Meccano reading sheet and its section rail, but moves the rail into a gutter outside the sheet that exists only from wide screens up, and turns it into a thin sticky progress strip under the header on phones, pushing continuity with today's identity.

deviations.what: Overrides LongreadProse's figure, img and figcaption rules from the page with :global selectors: images become width auto, max-width 100%, max-height 80dvh on a centred card plate, with an uppercase spec caption beneath.
deviations.why: LongreadProse sets every img to width 100%, which upscales the 192 by 256 logo to the full measure. The production fix belongs in LongreadProse.

deviations.what: HeaderProgressStrip moves its own DOM node into the fixed Header with a use: action, and sits absolutely positioned on the header's bottom edge.
deviations.why: Header has no snippet for content under its bar, and a strip sticky just below the header would sit over the text scrolling beneath it. Production needs a Header slot rather than the DOM move.

deviations.what: Below 80rem a sticky pill berth (a 64px band of page ground with a short fade above it) sits at the foot of the screen for the agent pill to rest on, so text leaves view before it reaches the pill.
deviations.why: On a phone no column can step around a box fixed to the viewport. The AT-077 shoot.mjs check is geometric and blind to clipping, so at 375 it still lists the berth and the pill for paragraphs passing behind the berth, as it would list the header if it did not exclude it.

deviations.what: Uses LongreadArticle with showProgress={false} and measures the reading position itself (Page plus readingProgress.ts), duplicating LongreadArticle's active-section tracking.
deviations.why: LongreadArticle keeps its active index private and draws only its own fixed left rail, so the gutter rail and the header strip cannot read it.

approaches.title: Contents margin
approaches.direction: Uses a two-column grid on desktop with a sticky contents aside and captions set in the margin beside their figures, collapsing to one column with a collapsible contents block at the top on phones, pushing structure and the grid.

deviations.what: Own CSS grid (grid-template-areas: contents, back, hero, body, after) instead of MainLayout.
deviations.why: MainLayout renders a second <main> inside PageFrame's <main>, its flex row cannot host the third margin-lane track the captions need, and its default stickyTop ignores the fixed header. Production would need MainLayout to render a div and accept a third track, or a dedicated article grid layout.

deviations.what: :global override of LongreadHero to start alignment (text-align, padding, standfirst margin).
deviations.why: LongreadHero is hard-centred; this approach puts title, standfirst and lede on one left line of the grid. Production would need an align prop on LongreadHero.

deviations.what: :global overrides of LongreadProse image and figure rules: img width auto, max-width 100%, max-height 75dvh; figcaption moved into the margin lane on wide screens by making the figure a two-track grid that reaches across the lane with a negative right margin.
deviations.why: LongreadProse forces img width 100%, which upscales the 192 by 256 logo into a red block, and has no caption placement option. Production would need LongreadProse to size images to content and cap them at the viewport, plus a caption placement option (below or margin).

deviations.what: A sticky bottom band (pill-foot) on phones only, 64px of page surface with a hairline, which text scrolls beneath; shoot.mjs therefore reports pill-foot and the pill stand-in as overlapping paragraph boxes at 375.
deviations.why: At 375 the pill spans half the column, so no text layout alone can keep scrolling lines out from under it; the band reserves the strip the pill sits on, the way the header reserves the top, so no visible word is under the pill. The overlap is box geometry against text hidden by the band, not text the pill covers. From 48rem up the band is gone and the pill sits under the contents column.

deviations.what: Literal rem track widths on the grid (13rem contents, 40rem measure, 12rem margin lane) declared as local custom properties.
deviations.why: Alfons has no measure or column-width tokens; LongreadProse itself hard-codes a 42rem measure. A production version would want measure tokens.

approaches.title: Figures lead
approaches.direction: Lets figures break out of a narrow text column to a wider measure on desktop, capped at the viewport height and framed with their captions, with a hairline reading-progress bar as the only navigation, pushing images and the cinematic end of the system.
deviations: a4/ReadingProgress.svelte reaches into ProgressBar's internals with :global(.motif-progress-track) and :global(.motif-progress-fill) to thin the track to a 2px hairline with no visible track and to drop the 0.4s fill transition. ProgressBar's smallest size is 5px and its fill lags a scroll, so a reading bar cannot be built from its public props; production wants a hairline size (or a reading variant) on ProgressBar instead of this override.

Figures are lifted out of the sanitised section HTML (a4/scenes.ts) and rendered as LongreadFigure elements between LongreadProse runs, instead of passing each section whole to LongreadProseSection. LongreadProseSection keeps everything inside the 42rem prose column, so a figure cannot break out to a wider measure through it; production would move this split into the server renderer beside the figure pairing.

approaches.title: Reading dock
approaches.direction: Gathers every floating control into one bottom reading dock on phones (contents sheet, progress and back) that clears the agent pill's corner and hides while scrolling down, pushing interaction so that nothing floats over the text while reading.
deviations: Below 80rem the article scrolls inside a fixed reading viewport (.reading-viewport) that stops above a reserved floor band, instead of the document scrolling. Why: the agent pill is fixed bottom-left over the full-width phone column, so the only way text never sits under it (or under the dock beside it) is for the scrolling region to end above that band. Costs: mobile browser chrome no longer collapses on scroll, scroll restoration and window-scroll listeners (Header) see no scroll, and the box-based overlap check flags paragraph boxes that continue below the viewport's clip edge even though that part is clipped and invisible.

The floor's height and the dock's left clearance are measured from the agent pill at runtime (getBoundingClientRect), not tokens. Why: the pill belongs to the agent dock and has no token for its geometry; measuring keeps the band right if the pill changes.

The page overrides LongreadProse's img rule through :global (width:auto, max-width:100%, max-height:70dvh, centred figure and caption). Why: LongreadProse sets img width:100%, which upscales the 192x256 logo into a measure-wide block; the production fix belongs in LongreadProse itself.

Literal layout sizes: an 80rem breakpoint (duplicated in Page and ReadingFloor), a 14rem margin-dock track mirrored on the right, a 42rem measure track matching LongreadProse's own max-width, and a 70dvh image cap. No breakpoint, track or measure tokens exist for these.

LongreadArticle is used with showProgress={false} only as the article axis; its section-focus observer runs but drives nothing, because the dock needs the active section outside the article (in the floor and in the sheet) and the library context does not expose it. The page runs its own scroll measurement instead.

approaches.title: Rail on desktop, dock on phones
approaches.direction: Simon's choice on 2026-10-30, combining his own lamp rail on today's raised sheet from 80rem up with approach 5's reading dock below it, so the rail is kept as designed where it never touches text and phones get the dock.
deviations: Everything a5 records for the phone dock carries over unchanged: the inner reading viewport below 80rem, the pill-measured floor, the LongreadProse image override and the 80rem breakpoint.

From 80rem the sheet and the rail's lamp styling are page CSS restyling LongreadArticle's internal .progress-rail, .rail-square and .rail-label through :global, copied from Atlas's EditorialDocument. Why: LongreadArticle has no sheet-edge placement or lamp variant; promotion should give it one so the page stops reaching into its internals.

The rail's boundary (centred until the sheet's foot reaches it, then travelling with the sheet) is a page effect, as in EditorialDocument. Why: LongreadArticle's rail is fixed to the viewport and knows nothing of the container it belongs to.
Literal 51.5rem sheet width and 5rem side padding, kept from today's sheet. No measure or sheet-padding tokens exist.
